jobs.excerpt: About SimpliFedSimpliFed is a virtual maternal health company.
jobs.description:
About SimpliFed

SimpliFed is a virtual maternal health company. We start with feeding support (lactation care, pumping and supply help, and prescribing for breast pumps and related needs) and build from there into care across pregnancy and postpartum, including postpartum mood screening and connection to the right next level of care. Our clinicians see families by video across the U.S., working alongside health plans, health systems, and breast pump suppliers.

We believe the key to every happy, healthy baby is a happy, healthy parent.

How we think about feeding

We help families feed their babies in whatever way works for them: nursing, exclusive pumping, formula, combination feeding, donor milk, supplementing, or weaning. Our job is to give parents accurate information and real support for their goals, not to judge their choices. A confident, supported parent and a fed, growing baby are the outcomes we care about.

We hire clinicians who share this view and show it in how they talk with families.

The role

You'll see new and expecting parents in live video visits, mostly to evaluate and order breast pumps and related supplies, plus feeding-related prescribing when it's clinically appropriate. Visits are short (about 20 minutes including documentation), same-day, and patient-facing, not chart review. You'll work alongside our IBCLC and RN/IBCLC team, who carry families' ongoing lactation care. This is our fastest-growing service line.

What you'll do

  • Run live video visits: history, assessment, and orders for breast pumps, supplies, and feeding-related medications when appropriate.
  • Document medical necessity clearly. Your note is what supports the order with the health plan and the supplier.
  • Bring a feeding-informed lens to each visit and hand families to our lactation team for ongoing support.
  • Run prenatal and postpartum video visits covering feeding assessment, latch and positioning, milk supply, pumping and flange fit, supplementing, bottle feeding, formula transitions, and weaning.
  • Build practical care plans around each family's own feeding goals.
  • Screen for postpartum and infant red flags and escalate or refer per SimpliFed protocols.
  • Maintain your state licenses and health plan enrollment; complete our EHR and e-prescribing training.
  • Follow up with families and our lactation team as needed after visits.

Required

  • Active, unrestricted NP/APRN, CNM, or PA-C license with prescriptive authority in at least one U.S. state. See our priority states below.
  • Available at least 15 hours a week. 20+ hours preferred.
  • Willing to practice under a collaborative or supervisory agreement where your state requires one. SimpliFed arranges the physician; you don't need to bring your own.
  • A private, quiet space for video visits, reliable high-speed internet, and a computer with a camera that meets our telehealth platform requirements.

Preferred

  • The same days and times each week (fixed weekly blocks).
  • A license in Texas (our top priority), North Carolina, or Pennsylvania, or licenses in several states.
  • Women's health, midwifery, family, or pediatric background (WHNP, CNM, FNP, PNP).
  • IBCLC or CLC certification.
  • Telehealth, DME, or outpatient prescribing experience.
  • An individual NPI, an active CAQH profile, and current enrollment with UnitedHealthcare, BCBS/Anthem, Aetna, or Cigna.
  • Illinois NPs: Full Practice Authority on file.
  • Evening or weekend availability, and able to start onboarding within 30 days.

Where we're hiring

We hire against measured patient demand and our current coverage gaps.

Priority

States

1. Highest need

Texas

2. High need

North Carolina, Pennsylvania

3. Helpful

Maryland, Illinois

Other states

We welcome NPs licensed elsewhere. We're building our pipeline for 2027 and will reach out as those states open.

Schedule and commitment

We're moving away from a large panel of low-hour contractors toward fewer, more committed providers per state. It cuts credentialing overhead for everyone and gets families seen faster. We look for at least 20 hours a week of availability. Providers who can offer the same days and times each week, and more hours, get priority scheduling and more volume.

Getting started

After you accept an offer, you'll complete a 30-day onboarding period: credentialing, systems setup, and training. Our aim is to have you seeing families as soon as that 30 days is done.

Credentialing with licensing boards and health plans can take 30 to 90 days from your hire date to delivering care, depending on your licenses and which health plans you'll see patients under. We'll tell you up front what to expect for your situation and start the paperwork the day you accept.

Pay

Hourly rates for 1099 contract roles, by regional market tier (based on where you live):

  • Tier 1 (CA, NY, MA, NJ, HI, MD): $75–$80/hr
  • Tier 2 (IL, CO, OR, VA, PA, AZ, MN): $66–$70/hr
  • Tier 3 (NC, GA, FL, TX, TN, OH, MI, IN, SC, WI, MO, and states not listed): $60–$64/hr
  • Tier 4 (MS, AR, WV, KY, OK, AL, LA): $54–$58/hr

Part-time and full-time W2 roles are also available for clinicians who commit to more hours.

Overview

DecisionPoint is seeking an experienced Business Analyst to support an assigned software application within the MODES III environment. This individual will serve as the primary bridge between the government customer and the software development team, translating mission and business needs into clear, actionable requirements and helping drive those requirements through development, testing, release, and adoption.

The Business Analyst will also perform Scrum Master responsibilities for the assigned application team. The role facilitates Agile ceremonies, maintains delivery visibility, helps remove impediments, and keeps the development team aligned with sprint goals and customer priorities.

This is a hands-on, customer-facing role. The successful candidate must be comfortable leading requirements discussions, working directly with government stakeholders, collaborating daily with developers and testers, and taking ownership of work from initial discovery through successful delivery.

This position is fully remote.

Duties & Responsibilities

Business Analysis and Requirements

  • Work directly with government customers, Product Owners, subject-matter experts, and users to understand mission needs, business processes, pain points, and desired capabilities.
  • Lead discovery sessions, stakeholder interviews, requirements workshops, and requirements reviews.
  • Translate business needs into clear user stories, functional requirements, acceptance criteria, workflows, process maps, and supporting documentation.
  • Understand and document the business problem behind a request rather than simply recording the requested solution.
  • Identify requirement gaps, dependencies, risks, assumptions, and conflicting stakeholder needs early in the development lifecycle.
  • Maintain requirements traceability from business need through development, testing, user acceptance, release, and implementation.
  • Partner with developers, UX/UI designers, QA, cybersecurity, cloud, and other technical teams to confirm that requirements are complete, testable, and technically feasible.
  • Support user acceptance testing, release readiness, release notes, user guidance, demonstrations, and implementation activities.

Scrum Master and Agile Delivery

  • Perform Scrum Master responsibilities for the assigned software application and development team.
  • Facilitate sprint planning, daily stand-ups, backlog refinement, sprint reviews or demonstrations, and retrospectives.
  • Partner with the Product Owner and government customer to maintain a healthy, prioritized, and delivery-ready product backlog.
  • Ensure user stories have sufficient context, acceptance criteria, dependencies, and supporting information before entering development.
  • Track sprint commitments, impediments, dependencies, risks, carryover, and follow-up actions.
  • Help remove obstacles affecting the team’s ability to deliver while escalating issues that require program or government action.
  • Protect the development team from unclear requirements and uncontrolled scope changes during an active sprint.
  • Promote continuous improvement, team accountability, transparency, and practical Agile practices.
  • Use Jira and Confluence, or approved equivalent tools, to manage the backlog, requirements, decisions, Agile artifacts, and team documentation.

Government Customer and Development Team Partnership

  • Serve as a trusted day-to-day partner to the government customer for the assigned application.
  • Develop a strong understanding of the application’s mission, users, business processes, priorities, and technical environment.
  • Translate between business and technical language so the government customer and development team share a clear understanding of what is being built and why.
  • Lead conversations when requirements are incomplete, ambiguous, conflicting, or technically challenging.
  • Communicate progress, risks, dependencies, decisions, and delivery concerns clearly and professionally.
  • Coordinate continuously with developers and testers rather than treating requirements as a one-time handoff.
  • Lead or support customer demonstrations, sprint reviews, requirements reviews, and release discussions.

Team Contribution and Mentoring

  • Share business analysis and Agile best practices with other Business Analysts.
  • Mentor less-experienced Business Analysts when opportunities arise.
  • Peer review user stories, requirements, acceptance criteria, workflows, and other BA deliverables.
  • Contribute reusable templates, standards, and lessons learned that improve consistency across application teams.
  • Participate in BA knowledge-sharing sessions and cross-team collaboration.

Qualifications

  • Active Secret clearance required.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Information Technology, Computer Science, Systems Engineering, or a related field. Relevant additional experience may be considered in lieu of a degree when permitted by the contract.
  • Five (5) or more years of experience in Business Analysis, Systems Analysis, Product Management, or a related software-delivery role.
  • Demonstrated experience gathering and documenting requirements for software applications.
  • Experience writing user stories, acceptance criteria, functional requirements, workflows, and process documentation.
  • Experience facilitating customer requirements sessions and technical discussions.
  • Experience working directly with software developers, QA professionals, Product Owners, and government or enterprise stakeholders.
  • Hands-on experience in an Agile or Scrum software-development environment.
  • Experience facilitating Scrum ceremonies or performing Scrum Master responsibilities.
  • Experience with Jira and Confluence, Azure DevOps, or comparable lifecycle-management tools.
  • Strong written, verbal, facilitation, presentation, analytical, and organizational skills.
  • Ability to work independently, manage competing priorities, and drive ambiguous requirements toward resolution.
  • Active Secret clearance supported by the required background investigation, when required by the position.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience supporting DoW or other federal software applications.
  • Experience with enterprise case-management, workflow-driven, or citizen- and family-facing applications.
  • Experience supporting application modernization, greenfield software development, or complex system integrations.
  • Working knowledge of APIs, databases, integrations, accessibility requirements, cybersecurity considerations, and modern web application architecture.
  • Experience planning or supporting UAT, application releases, user adoption, and customer demonstrations.
  • Practical experience operating in a hybrid fixed-price and time-and-materials contract environment.

Certifications

Agile, Scrum, Product Owner, or Business Analysis certifications are preferred but not required. Relevant credentials include:

  • Professional Scrum Master I (PSM I) or Certified ScrumMaster (CSM)
  • Certified Scrum Product Owner (CSPO) or Professional Scrum Product Owner I (PSPO I)
  • PMI Professional in Business Analysis (PMI-PBA)
  • IIBA Entry Certificate in Business Analysis (ECBA), Certification of Capability in Business Analysis (CCBA), or Certified Business Analysis Professional (CBAP)
  • ITIL 4 Foundation or equivalent service-management certification

Selected candidates may be required to complete employer-sponsored Agile, Scrum, or Product Owner training or certification after hire. DecisionPoint may provide CSPO or comparable training to establish a consistent approach to product vision, stakeholder engagement, value prioritization, and backlog management across application teams.

Our Equal Employment Opportunity Policy

It is the policy of DecisionPoint Corporation to provide equal employment opportunity in accordance with all applicable Equal Employment Opportunity/Affirmative Action laws, directives and regulations to all employees and qualified applicants without regard to race, ethnicity, color, religion, national origin, sex, age, disability status, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, genetic information, protected veteran status, or any other protected status under Federal, State or Local laws.

WHO WE ARE

Elliott Davis pairs forward-thinking tax, assurance and consulting services with industry-leading workplace culture. Our nine offices — located in the fastest growing cities in the US — are built on a foundation of inclusivity, collaboration, and collective growth. We work daily to provide exceptional service to our people, customers, and our communities. Audit and assurance services are provided by Elliott Davis, LLC(doing business in NC and D.C. as Elliott Davis, PLLC), a licensed CPA firm.

About the Role

The Elliott Davis State and Local Tax (SALT) practice helps businesses navigate the increasingly complex state and local tax environment. Our team combines deep technical knowledge with a practical, client-focused approach to help companies manage risk, improve compliance, identify tax savings opportunities, and make better business decisions.

We are seeking a Sales and Use Tax Manager to join our growing SALT practice. This individual will lead sales and use tax advisory engagements, manage client relationships, develop and mentor team members, and help identify opportunities to expand our work with both existing and prospective clients.

This is an opportunity for an experienced sales and use tax professional who enjoys solving complex tax issues and wants to operate as a trusted advisor to clients rather than focusing solely on compliance.

What You Will Do

  • Lead and manage multiple sales and use tax advisory engagements across a diverse client base, including manufacturers, distributors, technology companies, service businesses, and other multistate organizations.
  • Advise clients on complex sales and use tax matters, including taxability, nexus, sourcing, exemptions, marketplace issues, registration requirements, and multistate compliance.
  • Identify tax savings and planning opportunities, including sales and use tax refund reviews, reverse audits, exemption opportunities, and process improvements.
  • Conduct and oversee multistate nexus and taxability studies and translate technical findings into practical recommendations for clients.
  • Assist clients with sales tax audits and controversy matters, including responding to information requests, evaluating assessments, developing technical positions, and working with state taxing authorities.
  • Evaluate clients' sales and use tax processes and recommend improvements related to data, systems, exemption certificate management, and tax determination.
  • Work with sales tax technology solutions such as Avalara and Vertex and assist clients with technology implementation, optimization, and related process improvements.
  • Research complex state and local tax issues and prepare or review technical memoranda, taxability analyses, matrices, client correspondence, and other deliverables.
  • Manage engagements from planning through completion, including project scope, budgets, staffing, deadlines, billing, and overall client communication.
  • Develop strong client relationships and serve as a trusted resource for finance, tax, accounting, and operational teams.
  • Identify opportunities to expand relationships with existing clients and collaborate with other Elliott Davis professionals to bring appropriate SALT and broader firm resources to clients.
  • Participate in business development, proposals, prospect meetings, presentations, and thought leadership activities.
  • Coach, supervise, and mentor SALT professionals, providing technical guidance and helping develop the next generation of the practice.
  • Collaborate across the broader SALT practice on income and franchise tax, credits and incentives, property tax, unclaimed property, and other multistate matters when appropriate.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, Taxation, Business, or a related field.
  • Approximately 5+ years of relevant sales and use tax or state and local tax experience, preferably with a public accounting firm, consulting firm, corporate tax department, or state taxing authority.
  • Strong technical knowledge of multistate sales and use tax concepts, including nexus, taxability, exemptions, sourcing, and compliance.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage multiple engagements and client relationships simultaneously.
  • Demonstrated ability to identify and develop new client opportunities and expanded service opportunities within existing relationships.
  • Strong research, analytical, written, and verbal communication skills.
  • Experience reviewing the work of others and providing technical guidance to professional staff.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Excel, Word, PowerPoint, and Outlook.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Master's degree in Accounting, Taxation, or a related field.
  • CPA, JD, or CMI, Sales Tax designation from the Institute for Professionals in Taxation (IPT), or progress toward an applicable professional credential.
  • Experience with sales and use tax technology platforms such as Avalara, Vertex, or similar tax automation solutions.
  • Experience conducting reverse audits, refund reviews, nexus studies, taxability studies, voluntary disclosure agreements, and audit defense.
  • Experience working with multistate businesses in industries such as manufacturing, distribution, technology/SaaS, construction, or professional services.
  • Experience managing and developing professional staff.

What Success Looks Like

A successful Sales and Use Tax Manager at Elliott Davis will be able to combine technical expertise, project leadership, client service, and commercial awareness. The Manager will not simply identify what the tax law says, but help clients understand what it means for their business, what risks or opportunities exist, and what they should do next.

The Manager will also play an important role in growing the SALT practice by developing team members, strengthening client relationships, identifying new opportunities, and helping Elliott Davis continue to build a highly regarded multistate tax advisory practice.

WHY YOU SHOULD JOIN US

We believe that when our employees are able to thrive in all facets of life, their work and impact are that much greater.
That's right – all aspects of life, not just your life as an employee, because we understand that there's life beyond your job. Here are some of the ways our work works for your life, your growth, and your well-being:
• generous time away and paid firm holidays, including the week between Christmas and New Year’s

• first-class health and wellness benefits, including wellness coaching and mental health counseling

NOTICE TO 3RD PARTY RECRUITERS

Elliott Davis will not be responsible for, or owe any fees associated with, referrals of those candidates and/or for submission of any information, including resumes, associated with individuals.

Who are we?

Hi! 👋 We are Ravelin! We're a fraud detection company using advanced machine learning and network analysis technology to solve big problems. Our goal is to make online transactions safer and help our clients feel confident serving their customers.

And we have fun in the meantime! We are a friendly bunch and pride ourselves in having a strong culture and adhering to our values of empathy, ambition, unity and integrity. We really value work/life balance and we embrace a flat hierarchy structure company-wide. Join us and you’ll learn fast about cutting-edge tech and work with some of the brightest and nicest people around - check out our Glassdoor reviews.

If this sounds like your cup of tea, we would love to hear from you! For more information check out our blog to see if you would like to help us prevent crime and protect the world's biggest online businesses.

The Team

You will be joining the Detection team. The Detection team is responsible for keeping fraud rates low – and clients happy – by continuously training and deploying machine learning models. We aim to make model deployments as easy and error free as code deployments. Google’s Best Practices for ML Engineering is our bible.

Our models are trained to spot multiple types of fraud, using a variety of data sources and techniques in real time. The prediction pipelines are under strict SLAs, every prediction must be returned in under 300ms. When models are not performing as expected, it’s down to the Detection team to investigate why.

The Detection team is core to Ravelin’s success. They work closely with the Data Engineering Team who build infrastructure and the Intelligence & Investigations Team who liaise with clients.

The Role

We are currently looking for a Data Scientist to help train, deploy, debug and evaluate our fraud detection models. Our ideal candidate is pragmatic, approachable and filled with knowledge tempered by past failures.

Evaluating fraud models is hard; often times we do not even get labels for 3 months. You’ll need to use your judgement when investigating cases of ambiguous fraud and when you’re investigating the veracity of the model itself.

We have to build robust models that are capable of updating their beliefs when they encounter new methods of fraud: our clients expect us to be one step ahead of fraud, not behind. You will be given the equipment, space and guidance you need to build world class fraud detection models.

The work is not all green field research. The everyday work is about making safe incremental progress towards better models for our clients. The ideal candidate is willing to get involved in both aspects of the job – and understand why both are important.

Key Responsibilities

  • Build out our model evaluation and training infrastructure.
  • Develop and deploy new models to detect fraud whilst maintaining SLAs
  • Write new features in our production infrastructure
  • Research new techniques to disrupt fraudulent behaviour
  • Investigate model performance issues (using your experience of debugging models).

Requirements

  • Around 1 year's experience building and deploying ML models using the Python data stack (numpy, pandas, sklearn or pytorch).
  • Strong analytical skills.
  • Being a strong collaborator with colleagues outside of your immediate team, for example with client support teams or engineering.
  • Being skilled at communicating complex technical ideas to a range of audiences.
  • The ability to prioritise and to manage your workload.

Job description

Team & Reporting Line: Strategy Team, reporting to CSO

Our Mission

At constellr, we're harnessing the power of space to solve one of Earth’s greatest challenges: climate resilience & security in a changing world. Our thermal satellite constellation delivers the most accurate land surface temperature data on the market, equipping commercial players, governments, defence agencies, and global institutions with the thermal intelligence they need to make strategic decisions – from national security and infrastructure to agriculture and climate resilience.

This is not a concept on a slide. Our first two SkyBee satellites have been in orbit since 2025, each flying a cryocooled thermal infrared instrument on a microsatellite, and our next satellites are already in the pipeline. Backed by a €37M Series A, we are now opening a new site in Munich to bring assembly, integration and test (AIT) in-house.

With offices in Brussels, Freiburg, Munich, Berlin and Toulouse, our multidisciplinary team of engineers, scientists and strategists is turning flight data from orbit into the next generation of thermal satellites.

Your Role

As Government & Strategic Partnerships Lead – Poland, you will lead constellr’s senior-level engagement with government, public authorities, defence organisations, space institutions and industrial partners across Poland.

This is an important, externally focused role requiring credibility, autonomy and an established regional network. You will represent constellr with senior stakeholders, develop trusted long-term relationships and support the identification, shaping and capture of strategic government and industrial opportunities.

Working closely with constellr’s executive, government, commercial, product and technical teams, you will ensure that Poland’s sovereign requirements, policy developments and partnership opportunities are translated into long-term strategic capability programmes for the region.

The role is remote and based in Poland, ideally Warsaw, with regular travel across the region and to constellr’s European offices, including Brussels and Munich.

  • Lead constellr’s government, prime and strategic partnership engagement within Poland and, over time, across the wider Central and Eastern European region.

  • Provide structured regional intelligence on policy, procurement, budgets, institutional developments and competitor activity.

  • Represent constellr at relevant industry events, government forums, conferences and bilateral engagements.
  • Support the development of long-term partnerships that strengthen constellr’s role within Polish, European and allied space and security ecosystems.
  • Ensure that all regional engagement is conducted in line with constellr’s legal, compliance, security and export control requirements.

Job requirements

About you

Required:

You are credible and confident within senior Polish government and industry environments, while being collegiate and effective in a fast-paced international organisation. You are politically astute, discreet and able to build long-term, trust-based institutional relationships, while being commercially minded, proactive and disciplined in execution.

You are motivated by complex missions with strategic, societal and security relevance.

Required:

  • Significant senior-level experience in government, defence, intelligence, space, security or a closely related industry.
  • A strong and relevant network across the Polish government, defence and industrial ecosystems.
  • Demonstrated experience engaging senior stakeholders within ministries, armed forces, government agencies or public-sector organisations on strategic programmes.

Why join constellr?

  • High-Impact National Security Mission: Be part of an ambitious mission to launch the world’s first commercial thermal infrared constellation, delivering sovereign-grade "behavioural" intelligence from space to close critical blind spots for defence, intelligence, and maritime surveillance agencies.

By leveraging modern, agile New Space methodologies, you will help design, build, and deploy dual-use thermal payloads into operational orbit at a speed and scale that traditional aerospace models simply cannot match.

  • Participate in project readiness reviews, safety meetings, and client discussions to identify hazards and confirm appropriate controls before work begins.
  • Review site documentation, including personnel training and certifications, orientations, required signage, safety data sheets, and project safety records.

jobs.description:
Who we are

Agility PR Solutions is a global leader in media intelligence and PR technology. Founded in 2003, we help communications teams around the world drive awareness, make smarter decisions, and protect their reputation when it matters most. Our enterprise-grade platform unifies media relations, media monitoring, social listening, AI visibility, and media intelligence into a single seamless system—turning overwhelming streams of coverage and conversation into decision-ready intelligence. Recognized for ease of use, results, and customer support, Agility is one of the most trusted names in media intelligence. Our mission is to empower the voices that shape the world's narratives, and we're looking for people who want to help us do it.

About the role

Reporting to the Associate Director, Demand Generation, the Performance Marketing Manager owns Agility's paid media investment and the performance of its campaigns, from audience and channel strategy through execution, optimization, measurement, and pipeline impact.

Paid search is a key component of Agility's MQL and go-to-market strategy, and this seat keeps it performing while the rest of the engine comes online. It runs paid search across Google and Microsoft, paid social with LinkedIn as the primary platform, retargeting across the web and social, intent-triggered advertising built on the buying signals we already collect from ZoomInfo and G2, paid placements on review and buyer platforms where they are available, and account-based display for the target accounts the sales development team is prospecting. It also leads conversion rate optimization for paid traffic — the landing pages, forms, and post-click paths that paid campaigns depend on — and brings that testing practice to the demand generation team's shared conversion experience. A paid click that lands on a page that does not convert is wasted twice.

The mandate has two halves that have to be true at once. Paid-sourced pipeline grows in absolute terms, in North America and in the UK, while cost per qualified lead falls and lead quality holds through to the Proposal stage and closed-won. And as organic and outbound channels scale, the share of MQLs that comes from paid declines because the other channels grew, not because paid shrank.

You work daily with the SEO, AI Visibility & Social Media Manager on search strategy (paid and organic search are one plan, and paid social is this seat's while organic social is theirs), the Field & Event Marketing Manager on webinar and event registration campaigns, the sales development team on speed-to-lead for paid conversions, the web developer and designer on landing page builds and tests, and Salesforce reporting that traces every campaign to closed-won.

What success looks like

  • Paid-sourced MQL volume grows quarter over quarter in both North America and the UK while blended cost per MQL falls.
  • Paid lead quality holds or improves: MQL-to-sales-accepted and meeting-to-Proposal conversion for paid-sourced leads are tracked by campaign and reviewed monthly with sales.
  • Retargeting, intent-triggered, and account-based advertising programs are live within the first 90 days and reporting on their own pipeline contribution.
  • Landing page and form conversion rates for paid campaigns improve measurably through a continuous testing program, with a documented test log and a win rate that justifies the next test, and the practice is adopted across the demand generation team.
  • Every paid dollar is attributable in Salesforce to pipeline and closed-won, and the paid media budget is reforecast monthly against return, not against spend.
  • The paid share of total MQLs declines over the year because organic and outbound grew, while paid volume itself still rises.

What you'll do — Paid Search & Paid Social

  • Own paid search end to end across Google and Microsoft: account structure, keyword and match-type strategy, negative keyword discipline, bidding, ad copy and extensions, and budget pacing across North America and the UK.
  • Run paid social with LinkedIn Campaign Manager as the primary platform: audience construction by segment and title, lead-gen and conversion campaigns, and disciplined tests on Meta, Reddit, and emerging or novel ad channels, with clear hypotheses, success criteria, and thresholds for scaling, iterating, or stopping.
  • Run paid placements on review and buyer platforms — G2, Gartner Peer Insights, Capterra, and equivalents — where paid opportunities exist, measured on the same return threshold as every other channel.
  • Coordinate search strategy with the SEO seat so paid and organic do not cannibalize each other, and so paid covers the terms organic cannot yet win.
  • Build and maintain campaign tracking in HubSpot — UTM standards, campaign objects, and lead source hygiene — so every paid lead arrives with its origin intact.
  • Stay current on developments and trends in paid media, emerging platforms, and new advertising opportunities, and proactively bring forward test ideas; stay equally current on Agility's own offerings so paid media reflects the latest agentic capabilities the product team is shipping.

Retargeting, Intent-Triggered & Account-Based Advertising

  • Build retargeting programs across the web, LinkedIn, and social that match message to funnel stage: visitors, content downloaders, webinar registrants, and open opportunities each see something different.
  • Turn intent signals from ZoomInfo and G2 into advertising audiences, so accounts researching the category or comparing us to competitors see Agility while they are deciding.
  • Run account-based display and social against the target account lists the sales development team is prospecting, so cold outbound and advertising reach the same accounts in the same window.
  • Evaluate ABM platforms against cost per sales-accepted meeting, and recommend one only when the pilot proves it; the existing intent and ad platforms are the starting point.

Conversion Rate Optimization & Landing Pages

  • Lead conversion rate optimization for paid traffic: landing pages, forms, demo-request and contact paths, and the post-click experience — and partner with the demand generation team on the shared conversion experience for organic, outbound, and event traffic.
  • Run a continuous testing program — headlines, offers, form length, page structure, proof placement — using analytics, heatmap and session tools, and a documented test log with results and next steps.
  • Work with the web developer and designer, with page copy supplied by the content team, to build and ship pages fast on the website and in HubSpot, with templates that let campaigns launch in days rather than weeks.
  • Instrument the full path in GA4, HubSpot, and Salesforce so conversion improvements are visible as pipeline, not just as form fills.

Measurement, Budget & Attribution

  • Own the paid media budget: monthly reforecasts, channel-by-channel return, and reallocation toward what is producing pipeline, with a written rationale for every shift.
  • Report weekly on spend, MQLs, cost per MQL, sales-accepted rate, Proposal-stage progression, and closed-won by channel, campaign, and market.
  • Audit campaign and landing page data quality so attribution is trusted by sales and finance, and flag discrepancies before they reach a forecast.
  • Use AI tooling for ad copy variants, audience hypotheses, and campaign QA, and hold automated campaign types to the same return threshold as everything else.

What you bring

  • 4+ years running B2B SaaS paid media hands-on, with personal ownership of a meaningful, multi-channel monthly budget — planning, pacing, and reallocating it yourself rather than supporting someone else's campaigns — and results you can describe by cost per qualified lead and pipeline, not by impressions.
  • Deep Google Ads and Microsoft Advertising expertise and strong LinkedIn Campaign Manager experience; working familiarity with Meta and Reddit as test channels and with paid placements on review and buyer platforms such as G2, Gartner Peer Insights, and Capterra.
  • Retargeting experience across web and social, and experience turning intent data (ZoomInfo, G2 Buyer Intent, or equivalents) into advertising audiences; ABM platform experience (6sense, Demandbase, RollWorks) is an asset.
  • A conversion rate optimization practice: you have run structured A/B and multivariate tests, can read GA4 and session or heatmap tools, and can build and edit landing pages in HubSpot or WordPress without waiting on a queue.
  • HubSpot and Salesforce fluency for campaign tracking and attribution, including UTM discipline and lead source hygiene.
  • Experience managing budgets across more than one market, ideally North America and the UK, with the judgment to pace spend to return.
  • A weekly numbers habit: you reforecast on data, cut what is not working, and can explain every reallocation in one paragraph.
  • Clear-eyed use of AI tools for copy variants and analysis, and healthy skepticism toward automated campaign types that hide their targeting.
  • Proven ability to write or contribute compelling ad copy and variations based on creative briefs, audience insights, campaign objectives, and messaging strategy.
  • Familiarity with PR, communications, or media intelligence buyers is an asset; a fast learner of a new buyer is required.

Why you'll love it here

  • Fully remote work environment
  • Collaborative culture – and key tools enabling it
  • Competitive compensation package
  • Health, Dental & Vision benefits
  • RRSP matching
  • Life Insurance
  • Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
  • Career Development & Progression opportunities
  • Paid Vacation, Personal Days and Sick days
  • Week off between Christmas and New Years'
  • No Internal Meetings Fridays

Location: United States

Shape where clinical trials can succeed before they even begin. As an SMM Feasibility Manager, you will turn site insights, clinical data, operational experience, and local market knowledge into recommendations that influence country and site selection for clinical trials. Working across global and local teams, you will assess feasibility, identify risks and opportunities early, and help establish realistic enrollment strategies. Your insights and ability to challenge assumptions will directly support faster study start-up, effective recruitment, and successful clinical trial delivery for patients.

Job Description

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead country-level feasibility assessments, translating site, patient, and operational insights into evidence-based recommendations.
  • Identify and evaluate potential sites using historical performance, local expertise, competitive intelligence, and relevant data sources.
  • Analyze feasibility findings to establish realistic site, patient enrollment, and study delivery commitments.
  • Identify risks and opportunities early, recommending mitigation strategies to strengthen study allocation, start-up, and recruitment.
  • Partner with study teams and site management/start-up colleagues to accelerate start-up and support effective recruitment planning.
  • Collaborate across global and local teams to influence study strategy, feasibility decisions, and successful execution.
  • Serve as the country feasibility subject-matter expert, appropriately challenging assumptions and escalating critical risks.

Essential Requirements

  • Scientific degree with relevant clinical trial, clinical development, or project management experience.
  • Minimum 5 years of relevant experience in clinical development, clinical operations, feasibility, study start-up, or a related pharmaceutical industry role.
  • Strong analytical and critical-thinking skills to translate feasibility data and site insights into clear recommendations.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead and influence effectively within complex, cross-functional and global matrix environments.
  • Working knowledge of clinical trial protocols, study design, and clinical development processes, with the ability to identify operational feasibility considerations and engage appropriate subject-matter experts when needed.
  • Excellent communication, negotiation, problem-solving, and conflict-resolution skills, with fluency in written and spoken English.

Benefits & Rewards

At Novartis, we’re committed to reimagining medicine together - and rewarding the people who make it happen.

In addition to your base salary, you may be eligible for a performance-based bonus depending on certain performance parameters.


Pay equity is a fundamental principle of our employment policy and reflects our commitment to create a diverse, equitable and inclusive environment that treats all employees with dignity and respect, as outlined in our Code of Ethics.

When you join Ergomed Group, you make a difference by helping to bring safe and effective pharmaceutical treatment to patients around the world. You’ll join a passionate and collaborative team of experts in clinical research, pharmacovigilance, and quality consulting.

We are diverse in many ways, yet our values unite us. Our values are how we work, not words on a wall. If they sound like you, you will feel at home here.

  • Quality: we hold ourselves to the standard patients deserve.
  • Integrity and trust: we do the right thing, especially when it is hard.
  • Drive and passion: we care about the outcome, because someone is waiting on it.
  • Agility and responsiveness: we move quickly, because patients cannot wait.
  • Belonging: everyone is welcome, and every voice counts.
  • Collaborative partnerships: we go further by going together.

We look forward to welcoming your application.

Medicine moves forward here. So will you.

Ergomed is a specialist clinical research organization focused on rare disease and select oncology indications. We partner with small to midsize biotech companies to move promising therapies through early phase development, so they reach the patients sooner.

We choose complex work on purpose. Rare disease and oncology trials carry real operational risk, and our people are experts at reducing it, protecting timelines, data quality and the experience of sites and patients at the same time. It is demanding, meaningful work, and no one here forgets that patients cannot wait.

That is why culture matters to us as much as capability. We have built a collaborative, international team where people share ideas, grow their careers and are trusted to take ownership early. With colleagues across North America, South America, Europe, Asia and Australia, we value teamwork, flexibility and a real commitment to work-life balance, because good science comes from people who feel supported.

If you want work with purpose, the agility to make an impact and a team that cares about the people behind the work as much as the work itself, we would love to hear from you.

jobs.description:
Job Description Summary

‎

At Castlight, we are looking for a Senior Manager, IT Security who operates as an impactful player-coach, bridging deep technical security execution with strategic, client-facing leadership. Reporting directly to the Head of Technology, you will lead a dedicated security team while actively contributing to GCP cloud and application security, supporting our internal audit team across SOC 2, HITRUST, and NIST, and championing our security posture to major employers and health plans. Whether you are guiding AppSec best practices, defending our architecture on a CISO call, or serving as the steady client bridge during an incident, you will be the guardian of the trust and systems that power healthcare journeys for millions of users. If you are a high-agency leader who thrives at the intersection of hands-on security engineering and executive commercial engagement, we want to talk to you.

‎

How will you make an impact & Requirements

‎

Who We Are:

At Castlight, we’re making it as simple as humanly possible for people to navigate the complicated, often frustrating, world of healthcare. We partner with America’s largest employers and health plans, transforming employee benefits into a deeply personalized and guided journey for millions of users. What we build genuinely helps people live happier and healthier lives.


What You'll Do:

Reporting directly to the Head of Technology, you will lead Castlight's dedicated security organization while driving customer-facing security trust and hands-on technical execution. Operating as a true player-coach, you will balance team leadership and strategic governance, direct technical and architectural execution, and client enablement and support.


In this role, you will:

  • Lead & Elevate the Security Team: Lead, coach, and support a dedicated team across SecOps, AppSec, CloudSec, and GRC—setting clear technical expectations, removing operational roadblocks, and fostering a culture of high agency and accountability.
  • Drive Security Operations & Automation: Oversee SecOps capabilities, including security automation (SOAR), infrastructure hardening, vulnerability management, and patch management coordination to strengthen the organization's overall security posture.
  • Champion Client Support & Sales Enablement: Partner with commercial, legal, and sales leadership to represent Castlight's security posture to prospective and current customers. Address security provisions in contracts, guide technical responses for complex RFPs, and lead security defense calls with client CISOs and risk teams.
  • Lead Customer Incident Communications: Serve as the primary, trusted technical bridge to customers when security issues or critical vulnerabilities arise—translating technical remediation into executive-ready communication alongside our CISO and Engineering leadership.
  • Execute Hands-on in AppSec & Cloud Security: Dive into technical reviews, guide AppSec standards across GitHub Actions and deployment pipelines, and shape secure cloud infrastructure patterns on Google Cloud Platform (GCP).
  • Support Auditability & Maintain Framework Standards: Partner closely with our internal audit team by embedding robust controls across engineering workflows, ensuring our technical architecture and operations continuously align with SOC 2, HITRUST, and NIST standards.
  • Drive Cohesive Incident Escalation & Response: Oversee vulnerability management and incident response escalations, coordinating closely with enterprise cyber operations to ensure swift containment, remediation, and recovery from emerging threats.
  • Establish Security Operations Metrics: Define and track key SecOps KPIs, including vulnerability remediation timelines, patch compliance, and security configuration drift, to measure operational effectiveness and drive continuous improvement.

Skills & Qualifications:

  • Leadership Experience: 7+ years of progressive information security experience, including demonstrated success leading, coaching, and mentoring technical security engineers in a player-coach capacity.
  • Client-Facing Acumen: Proven capability to interact directly with enterprise customer security leaders, procurement specialists, and health plan CISOs. Experience reviewing security contract terms, supporting enterprise RFPs, and articulating complex security postures to external stakeholders.
  • Technical AppSec & Cloud Depth: Hands-on experience with Application Security (DAST, secure SDLC, CI/CD pipeline controls) and Cloud Security architecture, with an emphasis on Cloud Platform (We run GCP - but any cloud platform is sufficient) and containerized/microservice ecosystems.
  • Security Framework Familiarity: Working knowledge of SOC 2, HITRUST, and NIST frameworks, with a track record of implementing technical controls and supporting auditability.
  • Crisis Management & Communication: Exceptional communication and presentation skills, with the ability to maintain composure during security incidents and clearly explain root cause, blast radius, and remediation roadmaps to client leadership.
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Demonstrated ability to partner effectively with Engineering, Product, Legal, and executive leadership, balancing defense-in-depth with business momentum.

‎

Peraton is a next-generation national security company that drives missions of consequence spanning the globe and extending to the farthest reaches of the galaxy. Each day, our employees do the can’t be done by solving the most daunting challenges facing our customers. Visit peraton.com to learn how we’re keeping people around the world safe and secure.

Responsibilities

Peraton is seeking a Service Level Agreement (SLA) Specialist to join our team of qualified and diverse individuals on our TSA IMPACT program.

The SLA Specialist is responsible for ensuring consistent service delivery performance through monitoring and analysis of SLA, SLO (Service Level Objective) and KPI (Key Performance Indicator) metrics, identifying trends and root causes, validating data accuracy, and driving corrective actions. The Specialist partners with technical teams, reporting teams, program leadership, and government stakeholders to support incident, change, configuration, and problem management processes.

Work Location: This position is fully remote.

  • Validate reported metrics and resolve calculation or reporting discrepancies with reporting teams and SLA or SLO owners.
  • Develop and maintain strategic improvement plans for underperforming SLAs and SLOs.
  • Collaborate with technical and business teams to drive continuous service improvements.
  • Coordinate with Peraton and government leadership on performance issues, corrective actions, and SLA strategy.
  • Serve as the liaison between technical teams, reporting teams, and customer stakeholders, including FEDSIM.
  • Test and validate new or modified reports and dashboards to ensure data integrity.

  • Experience analyzing data to identify root causes and performance trends affecting SLA compliance.
  • Understanding of the ITIL Incident Lifecycle Management process.
  • Experience collaborating with technical teams to implement corrective actions and improve service performance.
  • Experience testing and validating reports and dashboards in SharePoint, ServiceNow, or other systems.
  • Ability to define reporting requirements and support dashboard development.
  • Strong communication skills with the ability to interact effectively with senior leadership and government stakeholders.

  • Experience with one or more ServiceNow modules, including:
    • Configuration Management Database (CMDB)

    • Problem Management
  • Experience with the ServiceNow SLA module.

About Nutrient

At Nutrient, we're revolutionizing how the world works with documents. Our tools transform static files into intelligent, secure workflows, empowering businesses to innovate faster and smarter. Your Role at Nutrient…

As an Internal Tools Engineer with a strong focus on backend development, you will work on our applications, which power a lot of internal and external needs of the company, from product builds and licensing workflows to revenue analysis and operational management across Engineering, Sales, Product, and Finance.

These tools range from CLI tools written in Bash to a medium-sized Ruby on Rails application that provides our internal as well as customer-facing interface and connects to a variety of 3rd party systems, and serves AI agents via an MCP server. Our primary tech stack: Rails, Postgres, Terraform/AWS.

We are looking for an excellent collaborator who can solve problems independently and hold themselves to their own high standards. You will report directly to the COO and work as part of a small internal tools team, partnering closely with Engineering, Security and our go-to-market teams. If this is you, we want to hear from you.

What You’ll Work On…

  • Build and extend our core internal platform, a Ruby on Rails application for customer and license management, including the customer-facing features and release automation built on top of it.
  • Build and maintain reliable integrations between that platform and the business systems our teams depend on (CRM, support, project management and BI), so reporting and AI agents work from data people can trust.
  • Design and run the MCP servers and APIs that give AI agents governed access to company data and workflows: tool design, authentication and permission scoping, rate limits, observability, and evals that catch regressions.
  • Turn requests from Sales, Customer Success, Support, Product and Finance into working tools and automations, and help decide which ones are worth building.
  • Own security and compliance for the systems you run: SOC 2 evidence, penetration-test findings, and dependency and vulnerability updates.
  • Work as part of a small internal tools team: review each other’s code, share ownership of systems, and keep each other unblocked.
  • Be a manager of one, spending your time on whatever is most valuable at the moment.

What You’ll Bring...

  • A background in software engineering with a proven track record of independently driving projects from inception to completion.
  • Strong backend web development experience in a production framework (Ruby on Rails, Node, Python, Go or similar), plus shell scripting.
  • Deep understanding of databases and SQL (PostgreSQL).
  • Experience with managing and deploying backend services, including familiarity with containerization technologies and cloud platforms (Docker, Terraform, AWS).
  • Hands-on experience building with LLMs in production: tool use and function calling, MCP, context engineering, and using evals and transcript review to find and fix real problems.

Nice to have:

  • Experience designing systems for AI agents as users: clear tool schemas and descriptions, OAuth-based authentication and data scoping, and observability for model and tool calls.
  • API or integration work with Salesforce, Zendesk, Linear or similar business systems.
  • Experience with SOC 2 or other security compliance work.

Who Thrives Here…

At Nutrient, we’re not just hiring for skills. We’re hiring for mindset. The people who thrive here are:

  • Collaborators: You work openly, listen actively, and put team success first.
  • Hungry Learners: Rapid learning fuels your progress and career growth.
  • Curious Thinkers: You dig into the “why,” valuing understanding over simply being right.
  • Self-Starters: You take action without waiting for direction, turning obstacles into opportunities.
  • Owners: You take responsibility for outcomes and always look for ways to improve what’s in your control.
  • Doers: You focus on results, not activity, and want to know how your work moved the goal.

Why You’ll Love Working Here…

At Nutrient, we build tools that reshape how businesses and developers work with documents. Our culture is centered on continuous growth and collaboration. Every team member has room to learn, innovate, and drive meaningful impact.

  • A small team, not a solo seat: you’ll have teammates to review your work and think through hard problems with.
  • Your users are right next to you: the people who use what you build are our leadership team and colleagues in every function, so you see the impact of your work right away.
  • Systems that matter: licensing, release builds, and a data platform that our reporting and AI agents depend on every day.
  • Fully remote and async-first: minimal meetings, strong writing culture, and the independence to manage your own work.
  • Mission-critical product: Nutrient’s platform is trusted by 15%+ of the Global 500 across 80+ countries.
  • Strong growth trajectory: having more than doubled revenue over the past three years, backed by Insight Partners.

Nutrient believes in equal opportunity. jobs.description:
Brahma AI operates at the intersection of enterprise Media Asset Management (MAM) and cutting-edge generative media. We build and scale industry-leading generative AI models, including hyper-realistic digital humans (ATMAN) and multilingual voice synthesis (VAANI), for world-class enterprise clients in entertainment, sports, healthcare, and retail.

Role Overview
We are looking for a Security Engineer for Agentic AI to make the agents, tools, and models Brahma teams rely on safe by default. You will own the security of our sovereign agent gateway for model routing, MCP tool hosting, and multi-agent orchestration: how agents authenticate, what they can reach, how they handle untrusted input, and how every action is logged.

This is an application and AI security role, not a cloud security role. Our Cloud Security Engineer owns GCP, Kubernetes, network, and infrastructure-as-code posture. You own the controls above it, in agents, tools, models, and their data flows, and you share secrets, sandbox runtimes, and security telemetry with them. You work as part of a team led by the Lead Engineer for Agentic AI, together with the AI Architect , Senior Engineers, ML Engineers and Product Management. You also work closely with Security and compliance and other teams using or contributing to Agentic AI. You own and build the security controls; the Architect designs security into the architecture, and Senior Engineers build to your standards and fix findings in their components.

This is an individual contributor role: building controls, tooling, and tests, and reviewing code and designs. You also share security knowledge within the team and with other Brahma teams, so safe practices spread beyond the people who build the controls. You follow emerging agent and AI threats, test new attack classes in bounded experiments, and bring proven defences into production. Once they are live, you own them: monitoring, detection, and response in an enterprise environment. We assemble our setup from open protocols, open-source components, and our own services, so you build what is missing and maintain what you run. There is no formal on-call rotation yet, but one may be introduced.

Key Responsibilities

1. Threat Modelling & Secure Design

  • Agentic Threat Modelling: Threat model agents, tools, MCP servers, and multi-agent workflows using the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications, OWASP Agentic AI threats, and MITRE ATLAS, and run a lightweight pre-launch review gate.
  • Secure-by-Default Reviews: Review agentic code and designs, publish secure defaults, and make risk trade-offs explicit and owned.
  • Security Knowledge Sharing: Teach secure agent practices within the team and to other Brahma teams through guides, threat-model walkthroughs, demos and office hours.

2. Identity, Isolation & Guardrails

  • Agent & Tool Identity: Design authentication and authorisation for agents and tools with OAuth 2.0/OIDC, token exchange, and scoped, short-lived credentials, with per-tool least privilege, fail-closed MCP authorisation, and secrets kept out of agent runtimes.
  • Sandboxed Execution: Harden the containers and sandboxes where coding agents and tool calls run, with filesystem isolation, egress control, and human approval for irreversible actions.
  • Guardrails & Policy Enforcement: Build gateway defences against direct and indirect prompt injection, tool abuse, excessive agency, and data exfiltration: input and output filtering, PII/DLP, and policy-as-code, tuned so they do not stall developers.

3. Adversarial Testing & Supply Chain

  • AI Red-Teaming: Build an automated adversarial test suite (injection, tool misuse, exfiltration, goal drift) that runs in CI and on a schedule, so we can show controls work, not only that they exist.
  • Supply-Chain Security: Govern which MCP servers, skills, plugins, models, and dependencies we adopt, through review, allow-listing, signing, SBOMs, and scanning.

4. Detection, Response & Compliance

  • Audit Logging & Detection:Make every model, tool, and agent call traceable to a person and an agent, and feed guardrail events and anomalies into security monitoring and alerting.
  • Production Security Ownership: Own the security controls once they are live: monitor their effectiveness, tune guardrails from production data, and keep them patched and current as models, tools and standards change.
  • Incident Response & Compliance: Own the playbook for agent-related incidents and lead the technical response. Map controls to ISO 27001, ISO/IEC 42001, SOC 2, GDPR, and TPN, and keep evidence audit-ready.

Must Haves

  • Security Engineering Background: 5+ years in security engineering with a strong application or product security component, and fluent Python.
  • Build, Not Only Audit: Track record of shipping security tooling, controls, and automated tests as production code.
  • LLM & Agent Security: Hands-on experience securing LLM applications or agents against prompt injection and unsafe tool use.
  • Identity & Authorisation:Deep knowledge of OAuth 2.0, OIDC, token exchange, workload identity, and least-privilege design.
  • Threat Modelling:Experience leading structured threat modelling and turning findings into prioritised engineering work.
  • Secure SDLC & DevSecOps: Experience embedding security scanning and checks into CI/CD, and securing containerised workloads.
  • Risk Communication: Ability to explain risk and trade-offs clearly to engineers and leadership, and to document decisions.
  • Knowledge Sharing:Track record of teaching and documenting security practices for colleagues and other teams.

Nice to Have

  • AI Red-Teaming Tools: Experience with garak, PyRIT, promptfoo, or similar.
  • Policy Engines: Practical use of OPA/Rego, Cedar, or similar.
  • Sandboxing Technology: Familiarity with gVisor, Firecracker, seccomp, or Landlock.
  • Agent Infrastructure:Experience building or securing MCP servers, LLM gateways, or guardrail services.
  • GCP:Working knowledge of IAM, Workload Identity, Secret Manager, and Cloud Logging.
  • AI Governance & Media Security: Exposure to ISO/IEC 42001, NIST AI RMF, or MPA/TPN content security.
  • Certifications: OSCP, GIAC, CSSLP, or equivalent.

jobs.description:
The financial industry is growing at a record pace, but our data providers are still stuck in the past — with cumbersome onboarding processes, complicated APIs, slow infrastructure, and expensive licensing costs.

Databento is the market data platform for modern finance. The company provides real-time and historical data across futures, options, and equities through a unified API. By owning the entire market data stack end-to-end, Databento is the first platform of its kind to combine the performance and reliability demanded by the world's leading trading firms with a dramatically simpler developer experience. Our team includes alumni of Two Sigma, Citadel Securities, Flow Traders, IMC, Tower Research, Jump Trading, HRT, Jane Street, and SIG.

Events are where many of our customers, partners, and future hires meet Databento in person. They’ve grown from a part-time effort across the team into something that deserves a dedicated owner.

We’re hiring an Events Specialist to build and scale our events program and bring our brand to life. You’ll be the person who gives structure to how we run events and makes each one, from a quant meetup to a team off-site, worth showing up for.

You’ll take every event from initial concept through execution, managing budgets, vendors, logistics, and cross-functional coordination. Beyond execution, you’ll help shape our overall events strategy by identifying the right opportunities, evaluating their impact, and guiding where we invest our time.

Responsibilities
You’ll lead a growing portfolio of events across five programs:

  • Hosted events: Plan and run a regular series of meetups in key financial hubs to build our brand and connect us with customers, prospects, and the quant community.
  • Conferences and booths: Own our presence at industry conferences, from sponsorships and booth design to swag, shipping, staffing, and lead capture.
  • Client dinners: Organize dinners and small gatherings with clients and prospects, partnering with Sales, Growth, and Marketing to deepen relationships and support business development.
  • Campus strategy: Build and manage our campus presence, including career fairs, recruiting events, sponsorships, and student programs, to strengthen our employer brand and university relationships.
  • Team off-sites: Plan and coordinate off-sites for our fully distributed team, managing venues, travel, accommodations, and event logistics.

Across all of these, you’ll:

  • Set up and manage a centralized annual events calendar and budget, while identifying new opportunities.
  • Evaluate conferences, sponsorships, and hosted events against business objectives, expected impact, and return on investment, recommending which to add, prioritize, or cut.
  • Partner with Sales, Growth, Marketing, and People to ensure events support broader company objectives.
  • Coordinate with Marketing on invitations, promotion, and branded materials.
  • Source and negotiate with venues, caterers, hotels, printers, and AV vendors.
  • Manage travel and logistics for attendees and staff.
  • Build repeatable processes for event planning, execution, and post-event evaluation.
  • Track event performance, including attendance, leads, engagement, hires, and cost per attendee, to inform future investment.

Requirements

  • 3+ years of experience planning and running events, ideally across conferences, hosted events, and corporate or client events.
  • Demonstrated ability to take projects from concept through execution and build processes with minimal oversight.
  • Track record of juggling several events and competing deadlines without losing sight of the details.
  • Experience managing budgets, evaluating costs, and negotiating with vendors.
  • Strong project management skills and ability to coordinate across teams and stakeholders.
  • Data-driven approach to evaluating event performance, allocating budgets, and identifying improvements.
  • Clear written and interpersonal communication, plus a good eye for how an event looks and feels.
  • Comfort navigating ambiguity on a small, fully remote team.
  • Willingness to travel regularly, including internationally, with some evening events and occasional weekend travel.

Nice-to-haves

  • Experience with B2B, fintech, or trading industry events.
  • University relations or campus recruiting experience.
  • Experience building an events program or function from the ground up.
  • Familiarity with tools like Luma, HubSpot, Linear, and Figma.

We offer health, dental, disability, and life insurance benefits, as well as 401(k) matching for full-time employees. We accommodate 100% remote work, with teammates living around the globe and paid in their local currency.

The base salary range for this role is $70,000–$120,000, benchmarked to Tier 1 locations in each country. Total compensation may also include bonuses, commissions, and equity, depending on the role.

jobs.title: Senior Communications Officer- India Energy Program
jobs.excerpt: AboutThe International Institute for Sustainable Development (IISD) is a globally recognized think tank with more than 30 years of experience working to solve today's greatest sustainable development challenges.
jobs.description:
About

The International Institute for Sustainable Development (IISD) is a globally recognized think tank with more than 30 years of experience working to solve today's greatest sustainable development challenges. We combine deep expertise across critical policy areas with a collaborative approach to research, advice, and hands-on support that delivers real-world results. Headquartered in Winnipeg, Manitoba, we are a diverse team of over 300 experts working from offices in Canada and Switzerland as well as other locations around the world.

The position is based within the IISD Energy Program (), a rapidly growing team of over 60 experts based either in the IISD Geneva office or remotely in a range of countries, including India, Indonesia, and South Africa.

At an international level, our work program delivers cutting-edge research and practical policy support for energy policy reforms in developed and developing countries, including shifting public financial flows from fossil fuels to clean energy and implementing commitments to go beyond fossil fuels in a socially just way. We work closely with groups such as the Friends of Fossil Fuel Subsidy Reform, United Nations Environment Programme, International Labour Organization, World Bank, and World Trade Organization, as well as numerous civil society partners. Our approach is hands-on, through country-level research and outreach in India, Indonesia, South Africa, and Canada, as well as via international forums such as the G7, G20, United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), and Sustainable Development Goals.

In India, IISD has largely focused on the creation of knowledge and dialogue on government support for energy transition, including: data on subsidies for fossil fuels, renewables, and electric vehicles; how to sustainably reform consumer subsidies for liquefied natural gas, kerosene, and electricity; how to effectively subsidize clean energy, including solar irrigation, solar photovoltaic manufacturing, and electric vehicles; planning for a just transition; and how state-owned enterprises and public finance can better align with the energy transition.

We engage with government agencies at the central and state levels and partner with a wide range of national think tanks, academic institutions, and consultancies, including the Center for Study of Science, Technology and Policy, Council on Energy, Environment and Water, Climate Parliament, Consumer Unity & Trust Society, Indian Council for Research on International Economic Relations, Swaniti Initiative; Integrated Research and Action for Development, and The Energy and Resources Institute.

About the Position

The communications officer will lead communications for IISD’s Energy Program in India and South Africa. They will also closely collaborate with our international team working on UNFCCC and G20 processes to ensure voices from the Global South are represented in the Energy Program’s key messages and communications.

As a member of the wider Energy Program communications team, they will work closely with the communications manager and the digital senior communications officer, as well as the program’s India- and South Africa-focused policy experts.

The senior communications officer will be responsible for drafting and implementing the India and South Africa communications strategies for IISD’s Energy Program in these countries, advising the policy teams on communications best practices, as well as coordinating work with internal and external partners and agencies. They will write and edit editorial content related to the work of the program and use traditional and digital channels and tools to reach and engage target audiences. They are expected to be a highly independent, proactive professional, able to diligently track and schedule workload, produce polished outputs with minimal oversight, and drive early thinking on communications among policy research . They are also expected to collaborate with colleagues and other key stakeholders in the Civil Society Organisation (ecosystem in India and South Africa.

Their key areas of responsibility will include the following:

Creative Content

  • In consultation with the communications manager, draft, update, steer, and implement communications strategies for the India and South Africa work programs.
  • Inform, manage, and implement communications plans for a broad range of projects, reports, campaigns, and events. This includes crafting compelling narratives and talking points to articulate key messages, cooperating with internal and external stakeholders, ensuring timelines are adhered to, monitoring and evaluation, and reporting on impact.
  • Write, edit, and review written outputs (e.g., blogs, opinion pieces, press releases, social media posts) for framing, tone, and narrative, ensuring strategic and editorial consistency.
  • Regularly share program work and collaborate with IISD’s core communications team to ensure alignment on key messaging and amplification of programmatic expertise in broader, organization-wide communications activities. Contribute to a shared editorial calendar.
  • In consultation with policy staff, communicate with IISD’s donors to demonstrate how their support has made an impact.
  • Track current events and national energy policy movements in India and South Africa and globally related to specific workstreams, and identify opportunities for further work and/or public engagement.

Public Engagement and Social Media

  • Help inform and execute an email outreach strategy.
  • Oversee event-related outreach and post-event follow-up.
  • Inform the social media strategy and contribute to all active social media accounts, ensuring posts are relevant, timely, engaging, and targeted to the needs and interests of key audiences.

Media Relations

  • Engage with journalists and influencers, with a focus on relationship building; secure targeted coverage for IISD research and initiatives in key outlets in India and South Africa.
  • Draft, edit, and disseminate press releases, media briefings, and email pitches for reporters and editors. Draft or support other staff in writing and placing op-eds, media quotes, letters to the editor, etc.
  • Facilitate media training of IISD experts and support preparation ahead of speaking to the press, including developing and updating talking points and key messages.
  • Conduct regular media monitoring of relevant topics in Indian and South African media.

Digital Strategy

  • Working within content management systems such as Drupal or WordPress, upload and edit content for websites, adhering to IISD guidelines.
  • Ensure monitoring, assessment, and reporting on website traffic and engagement with its digital content, advising where appropriate on opportunities to improve.
  • In collaboration with IISD’s design team, draft and manage the production of digital content, including social media cards, posters, invitations, simple infographics, presentations, and other conference or workshop materials.

Internal Processes

  • Ensure brand coherence and compliance with existing IISD communications practices.
  • Manage internal processes related to the development and dissemination of communications products, including coordinating feedback from internal and external stakeholders, approvals, and copy editing.
  • Maintain strong relationships with program staff to gain a deeper understanding of their research and policy objectives and provide editorial guidance to IISD’s experts.

About the Successful Applicant

The successful applicant will be a highly skilled storyteller and communicator with experience in climate or energy-related communications and have a solid understanding of India’s climate and energy policies. Knowledge of South Africa’s energy context will be considered a plus. They will have extensive experience in media relations, with a proven track record of generating media impact. They will be confident in shaping communication strategies to reach and engage niche and highly targeted audiences. A good knowledge of international processes (UNFCCC, G20) will be considered a strong asset.

The successful applicant will also have the following qualifications:

  • A minimum of a bachelor’s degree or equivalent in a relevant field (e.g., communications, journalism, political science, economics, environmental or development studies).
  • 5 years of relevant work experience in journalism and/or communications.
  • Excellent oral and writing skills in English, with the ability to turn complex topics into engaging narratives for various audiences and a track record of written products in English.
  • Extensive experience in media relations in India. Additional experience with media in South Africa would be a strong asset.
  • Excellent organizational, planning, and project management skills.
  • Ability to prioritize and work quickly and accurately while being results-focused, with the flexibility to take on both highly complex and basic tasks.
  • A strong ability to work comfortably across different cultures and be inclusive and positive with different colleagues.
  • Strong computer literacy, including Microsoft Office applications, and experience in handling web-based communications and management systems, including WordPress, Mailchimp, and Google Analytics.

It is not required but will be considered advantageous if candidates can demonstrate

  • strong existing professional networks on energy and/or policy in India, and
  • prior experience engaging with state and central government officials on energy, environment, and climate change issues.

Location: The successful candidate must be based in Delhi, India. Candidates should also be comfortable with regular travel to support communications and engagement activities.

Candidates must hold an appropriate work authorization for locations where they expect to be based, without any sponsorship from IISD.

Salary: The target hiring range for this position is:

  • India: INR 1,949,304–INR 2,407,964 annually, with the opportunity to progress to a maximum of INR 2,866,624 annually.

Placement in the salary range will be based on factors such as market conditions, internal equity, and candidate experience, skills, and qualifications relevant to the role.

Type of employment: 100% full-time-equivalent staff position, including under an Employment of Record model. Two-year contract with a high possibility of extension.

Application Procedure

Applications will only be accepted through Bamboo HR.
